what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A coach sent a link to a product he could not sell: give people solutions, not problems.
sections.para: After a padel lesson a coach recommended a sleeve and could not sell it, which turned a question into a set of tasks. The lesson runs through business: a solution has a fair price set by the time and waiting it saves, transparency about the markup helps, an engineer beats a list of vulnerabilities, bookshops should always say yes, and RiskMandate's outreach has been handing people tasks without a clear return.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Give a solution, show what you add, and do not pass the ball back.
sections.para: The coach's link, the price of convenience, transparency, the security engineer, the bookshop, the travel agents, RiskMandate, and automating solutions with AI.

sections.label: The moment
sections.line: He knew the answer and had a customer who wanted to pay, and still sent a link.
sections.para: The buyer left with the same problem plus tasks: find a seller, check, order, wait. The answer hoped for was here it is, or tomorrow, at this price.

sections.label: Do not pass the ball back
sections.line: People want the problem solved, or their options with a recommendation, not next steps.
sections.para: A link is information; pay me and I will give it to you is a solution, and the easiest one to say yes to.

sections.label: The price of a solution
sections.line: A solution has a price, set by the time, trust and waiting it saves.
sections.para: There is a range where buying from the person in front of you is a no-brainer and a margin above which people do it themselves. The research on paying for convenience is thin: one 2018 UK study.

sections.label: Transparency is part of the solution
sections.line: Saying what you add widens the range; travel agents show what happens when you hide it.
sections.para: The US GAO called the old commission invisible to the consumer; online bookings rose from 7% to 30% of tickets in 1999 to 2002. Everlane and Costco built businesses on showing margins; Amazon's paid placements are the reverse case.

sections.label: In Wardley's terms
sections.line: Finding a seller is custom built; an offer with a price and a date is closer to a commodity.
sections.para: The friction is the gap between the two, and whoever closes it gets paid.

sections.label: The engineer, not the list
sections.line: A list of vulnerabilities is a problem; an engineer paid from the security budget is a solution.
sections.para: The worse the vulnerability, the bigger the problem it hands a team. Hiring engineers into teams changed the conversation and left teams better than found, the Boy Scout rule.

sections.label: The bookshop
sections.line: A bookshop's answer should always be yes, we can get it for you.
sections.para: Even with little margin it keeps the customer and the cash flow. UK independents reportedly order from wholesalers next day, and Bookshop.org shares margin with them.

sections.label: Where RiskMandate gets this wrong
sections.line: RiskMandate offers a way to control agents, then hands people a list of tasks.
sections.para: That is why the outreach is not working. The solution version would arrive with the first policy written and a control in place, as a service; that is a proposal.

sections.label: With AI, solutions scale
sections.line: Agents make the solution cheap enough to do every time.
sections.para: The shop, the link and the follow-up can be automated, as with every lesson becoming a sellable unit.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: The moment is the author's; the convenience research is thin; the FTC's points are allegations.
sections.para: The travel figures are from the US, and the RiskMandate service is a proposal.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: GAO, BLS, FTC, Amazon, Everlane, Costco, Wardley, 97 Things, Baden-Powell, Bookshop.org.
